clue.text: Absolute idiot on top of Ned Flanders's place

indicators.note: the top of a word in an across clue is its first letter, so this takes the opening letter of Ned

parts.note: a twerp is a silly, foolish person

explanation.surface: An insult aimed at Ned Flanders, the pious neighbour in The Simpsons, and the place where he lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ned Flanders' reads as the cartoon character, but Flanders is the Belgian region and the definition is a place in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Belgian port city lies in the Flemish region, so it is a place in Flanders.

clue.text: Light warning bank's not opened

indicators.note: a word not opened has lost its first letter

parts.note: camber is the banked slope across a road

explanation.surface: A notice that a bank has not opened its doors today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is a slope, not a place for money.
explanation.definitionFit: On traffic signals the middle, yellowish light warns drivers to prepare to stop.

clue.text: Demanding cyclist cycles — call to get going

parts.note: a tall order is a demanding one

indicators.note: cycling a word moves its letters round, here the last letter coming to the front

parts.note: Sir Chris Hoy is a British Olympic champion track cyclist

explanation.surface: An exacting cyclist rides off with a rallying shout.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry is the huntsman's shout on sighting the fox, urging the hunt to go.

clue.text: Senior official's vote in chamber's first up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read the result from bottom to top
in puts the vote inside the spelt-out letter

parts.note: the first letter of chamber is C, spelt out as the word cee
voters mark a cross, X, on the ballot

explanation.surface: A senior figure casts a vote first thing in the chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter C is written as its name, CEE; X goes in to make CEXE, which 'up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Exec is short for executive, a senior manager or official in a company.

clue.text: Last chance for ace?

parts.note: in tennis an ace is a serve the opponent cannot return, a point with no return

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a pilot's final chance; the tennis ace is a point that is never returned.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the stage after which turning back is impossible, the last chance to retreat.

clue.text: Beginning of bumpy roller coaster exposes boob

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so this takes the opening letter of bumpy

parts.note: a looper is a roller coaster that runs through loops

explanation.surface: A bumpy fairground ride leads to an embarrassing wardrobe malfunction.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is an informal word for a silly mistake, the same as a gaffe or slip-up.

clue.text: One that almost sailed may be fat with tobacco jars

indicators.note: to jar is to jolt, so the letters of may be fat and tobacco are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone might grow fat on jars of pipe tobacco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jars' looks like containers but is the verb, to jolt.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the online poll's winning name for a British polar research ship, which was given another name, so it almost sailed.

clue.text: Help to raise issue?

parts.note: issue means children: the exclamation is what people say when lifting a toddler who has fallen

explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise issue' reads as bringing up a point; here it is lifting up a child.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the comforting exclamation said when picking up a small child after a tumble.

clue.text: Impostors had to start among trapped animals

indicators.note: among puts the letter inside the animals

parts.note: ponies are the animals harnessed to a trap, a light two-wheeled cart

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so this takes the opening letter of had

explanation.surface: Fakes were caught among creatures that had been trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trapped' means harnessed to a pony trap, not caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonies are fakes, people pretending to be what they are not.

clue.text: They're temporarily on throne (on loo)

parts.note: re means on or concerning
the Gents is the British name for a men's public toilet

explanation.surface: A joke about people briefly perched on the throne, meaning the lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throne' slang for a toilet seat feeds the joke; the definition is a royal throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Regents rule on behalf of a monarch who is a child or absent, holding the throne for a time.

clue.text: Footballer in Arsenal trousers who practises first position?

indicators.note: used as a verb, to trouser is to pocket, so the words Footballer in Arsenal hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A footballer at Arsenal pockets his wages while working on his positional play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First position' is a ballet stance, not a place in a football team.
explanation.definitionFit: First position is the basic ballet stance with heels together, practised by every dancer of classical ballet.

clue.text: Tip for napping, post vacation

parts.note: pro means in favour of, so for

indicators.note: after vacating, napping is emptied of its middle letters, leaving only its outer ones

explanation.surface: Advice on taking a nap once the holidays are over.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong is the pointed tip of a fork or similar tool.

clue.text: Rose regularly, always welcomed light

indicators.note: welcomed means taken in, so one piece goes inside the other
taking letters at regular intervals from Rose gives its first and third letters

parts.note: ay (or aye) is an old word for always

explanation.surface: Someone rose early and always greeted the morning light.
explanation.definitionFit: Light reaches us as beams, so light can be described as a set of beams.

clue.text: Junk I can't say to leave at home

indicators.note: to junk something is to scrap it, so the letters of I can't say to are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to throw out rubbish and stays in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' is a noun here, a holiday from work.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a blend of stay and vacation: a holiday spent at home rather than away.

clue.text: Quickly finish drink by moving arm, set towards mouth

parts.note: to down a drink is to swallow it in one go

indicators.note: moving the letters of arm and set shifts them into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone knocks back a drink, lifting their arm to their mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouth' is a river mouth, not the drinker's.
explanation.definitionFit: Water flowing with the current heads towards the river's mouth, where it meets the sea.

clue.text: Escaped frequent fines

parts.note: to frequent a place is to go to it often
F stands for fine, as on pencil grades, so two fines give two Fs

explanation.surface: Someone avoided the many penalties they kept running up.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off is the idiom for escaping punishment or being let go.

clue.text: Frame Dave's mate — relatively finished!

parts.note: Chas is Dave's partner in Chas & Dave, the London singing duo
a relative cut short: sister clipped to sis

explanation.surface: Someone is framing a pal of Dave and declaring the job all but done.
explanation.walkthrough: Chas & Dave were a British cockney rock-and-roll duo popular from the late 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: A chassis is the base frame of a car or other vehicle.

clue.text: Chap from Santander's supply of loans

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, supply means flexibly, so the letters of of loans are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Santander, the Spanish bank, provides credit to its customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun but is the adverb from supple. Santander is a city in Spain as well as a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a typical Spanish man's name, borne by several Spanish kings, so it fits a man from Santander.

clue.text: Vote for right representatives of love

parts.note: voting for a party, one declares 'I am a' supporter
Tory is the name for Conservatives, the representatives of the political right in Britain

explanation.surface: Backing right-wing politicians as a gesture of affection.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'I am a Tory', the declaration of someone who votes for the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Amatory describes things relating to sexual love or lovers, like romantic poetry.

clue.text: Bulb one unexpectedly discovers!

definitions.meaning: a lamp or bulb that blinks on and off, as on a car indicator
discovers in the sense of uncovers: a man who suddenly exposes himself

explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovers' means uncovers, not finds.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a blinking lamp and an indecent exhibitionist.

clue.text: Supporting position of legal hooker?

definitions.meaning: on someone's side means backing or supporting them
a rugby hooker who is not offside is in a legal position

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about where a lawful prostitute stands.
explanation.walkthrough: The hooker is a rugby forward, not a sex worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporting means being on someone's side; in sport a player in a legal position is not offside.

clue.text: Moon was this close to asteroid, more suspect

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter, so this takes the final letter of asteroid

parts.note: rum means odd or suspect, so rummer is more suspect

explanation.surface: An astronomer's dubious claim that the Moon came very near an asteroid.
explanation.walkthrough: Moon is Keith Moon, the drummer of The Who, not the satellite.
explanation.definitionFit: Keith Moon played the drums for the rock band The Who.

clue.text: Man set trap that's crushed more than one flat

indicators.note: something crushed is squashed out of shape, so the letters of Man set trap are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A man laid a trap that was then squashed flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like the result of the crushing, but it is a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is a home on one floor of a building, also called an apartment, so several are the plural.

clue.text: Girl's large — you see why in audition

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

indicators.note: audition is hearing, so these words are to be heard rather than read

parts.note: the three words, said aloud, sound like the letters U, C and Y

explanation.surface: A big girl explains her reasoning at an audition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common girl's name, as in the Beatles song about a girl in the sky.

clue.text: Call when in range

parts.note: range here is a mountain range: the warbling call of Alpine herders

explanation.walkthrough: 'In range' sounds like a phone signal; the range is the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the warbling song with jumps between chest voice and falsetto, sung in the Alps.

clue.text: Guess marksman still finished

definitions.meaning: a guess is an attempt, as in 'have a go'
a good marksman is called a good one, as in 'a fine one with a rifle'
a still is a single photograph
finished as in worn out or ruined

explanation.surface: A marksman's guess that he is not done yet.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers an attempt, a skilled shooter, a photograph and the informal sense of exhausted.

clue.text: A shade closer to runner wearing sporty line

indicators.note: the line wears the letter, so it goes around it

parts.note: the oche is the line darts players stand behind to throw

indicators.note: the closer of a word is its last letter, so this takes the final letter of runner

explanation.surface: An athlete in a sporting kit gets nearer to the finishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closer' is the noun, the thing that closes a word, not the comparative of close.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a yellowish-brown earth pigment and the colour named after it.

clue.text: Buffet had menu, as open

indicators.note: to buffet is to batter, so the letters of had menu as are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A self-service meal had its menu on open display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' looks like the meal but is the verb meaning to knock about.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is not embarrassed acts openly, without shame or concealment.

clue.text: Harry and Mary — one of them works on the railway

definitions.text: one of them works on the railway

indicators.note: to harry is to harass, so the letters of and Mary are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A couple called Harry and Mary, one of whom has a railway job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name in the pair but is the anagram signal for the other five words' letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardman works in a railway yard, shunting and marshalling trains.

clue.text: Thrill of thirteenth rally

indicators.note: of signals a part taken from within, so the answer lies inside thirteenth rally

explanation.surface: The excitement of a motor rally in its thirteenth running.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrill someone is to captivate and delight them, as a gripping show does.
